title: donoteat this BONUS EPISODE 2: KILLDOZER!
premise: The presenter dismantles the viral folk-hero account of Marvin Heemeyer by reconstructing Granby’s property, planning and sewer disputes, arguing that accommodation and sanitary-waste requirements—not an inaccessible ruined business—preceded the destructive rampage.
coverage: Inspected all 39 original contact sheets and their 462 tiles, plus all four supplemental single-frame sheets (466 indexed frames across 43 sheets total). Original sampling: first available frame in every five-second bin plus FFmpeg scene-score >0.30 selections at 480px detection width. Read full timestamped machine-ASR transcript; full dialogue is source-derived by shared renderer, never authored excerpts. Camera/action descriptions rely on adjacent sampled frames; this is not continuous viewing and brief gags can be missed. Inspected four native targeted stills at requested 387.517, 696.2, 697.333 and 963.9 seconds. Registered and inspected portrait, CATHOLICS!, dust/noise-card and FINISHED SOME WORK supplements at actual source times 387.533, 696.2, 963.9 and 1363.733. Sound annotations identify metadata-documented music only with approximate section anchors; empty sound arrays mean unannotated, not silence.

panels.heading: Catholics: unrelated armed cutaway

sound.text: Spoken slogan, user-confirmed: “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”), after the deadpan “unrelated” in the Catholic/Irish-republican cutaway gag. Raw ASR incorrectly renders “Chucky R. Law,”; it is not a person. Coarse cue anchored to the first misrecognized source word at 698.36s, not independently measured audio onset. The gag is not an endorsement of the armed group.

panels.visualGag: Payoff to the preceding CATHOLICS! card: the ostensibly unrelated masked armed-group image redirects the Catholic-prejudice punchline toward an Irish-republican association, accompanied by the user-confirmed slogan “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”). The armed-woman photograph and explicit IRA graphic later repeat the same slogan/cutaway gag; not an endorsement of the armed group.
panels.notes: Native still inspected: visual/Yvl_7_Up7zU/targeted/at-697.333s.png. The user confirms the spoken phrase as “Tiocfaidh ár lá,” not raw ASR’s false-person rendering “Chucky R. Law,”. Raw word span 698.36–699.2s supplies the coarse annotation anchor; the user’s approximately11:37.5 reference introduces the sequence, not an independently measured slogan onset. Photograph subjects and original image source remain unknown; later explicit IRISH REPUBLICAN ARMY graphic establishes the running-gag association. Raw transcript remains unchanged; the correction sidecar supplies reviewed display wording.

panels.visualGag: Payoff to the blade/ripper feature catalogue: mundane window AC is an incongruous final amenity for an armored rampage machine; not proof this exact appliance was installed.

panels.heading: Poop bucket and old habits
panels.description: Game water/power information screens return over the modeled town.
panels.camera: Adjacent five-second samples show the game viewport changing position, scale and angle while editing; exact continuous camera path is not established.
panels.action: Information mode and asset selections change.
panels.visualGag: Spoken bucket/dump-in-ditch callback to the sewer dispute; the previous comfort panel becomes ironic because living quarters lack water/sewage. No bucket image was observed.

panels.heading: Cannot do the rampage in the game
panels.description: Game water view cuts to CBS4 archival aerial footage labelled BREAKING NEWS / Granby / EARLIER, showing armored dozer moving near another yellow machine.
panels.camera: Cut from game to aerial news video; adjacent samples show vehicle position changing.
panels.action: Dozer travels along roadway; source is edited archival footage.
panels.notes: Narrator admits inability to recreate this part in Cities: Skylines.

panels.heading: Catholic Church target: armed callback
panels.description: Black-and-white still of an armed woman with another person behind her interrupts the news video.
panels.camera: Abrupt cutaway then return to footage at 25:35.6.
panels.action: Static photograph.

sound.text: Spoken slogan callback, user-confirmed: “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”), again after “unrelated” with the Catholic Church/armed-woman cutaway. Raw ASR incorrectly renders “Chucky R. Law,”. Coarse cue anchored to source word start1533.7s; not independently measured audio onset. This repeats the Irish-republican gag, not endorsement of an armed group.

panels.visualGag: Callback to the first Catholic/Irish-republican cutaway: the Catholic Church target triggers another supposedly unrelated armed image and repeats the user-confirmed “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”) slogan; connects forward to the explicit IRA graphic and third slogan repetition. Not an endorsement of the armed group.
panels.notes: User-confirmed spoken slogan is “Tiocfaidh ár lá,” not raw ASR’s “Chucky R. Law,”. Raw word span1533.7–1534.64s supplies a coarse anchor, not independently measured audio timing. Photograph does not establish the individuals’ identities or original image source. Raw transcript is unchanged; reviewed display wording comes from the correction sidecar.

panels.heading: Scraper confronts the dozer
panels.description: News aerial view shows long yellow scraper and armored dozer close together along street.
panels.camera: Aerial tracking/reframing established by adjacent footage samples; precise path not reconstructed.
panels.action: Vehicles change relative position along the street.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the Docheff-name gag card in the next panel within a serious target-list narration.

panels.heading: Douche-eff
panels.description: Black title card reads DOUCHE-EFF.
panels.camera: Abrupt black-card cutaway.
panels.action: Static white text.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the target-list setup: narrator cites Heemeyer’s insulting spelling and dryly adds because of humor; card makes the juvenile nickname unmistakable.

panels.heading: Thirteen buildings and an attempted propane attack
panels.description: Aerial news footage returns, then shows armored dozer beside a red storefront with dust rising.
panels.camera: Cuts and aerial tracking; adjacent samples show approach and dust changes.
panels.action: Vehicle pushes into building edge; damage and dust follow.
panels.notes: Presenter’s propane-tank attempt claim is narrated; these frames do not identify a propane field.

panels.heading: Building parts are heavy
panels.description: Successive aerial frames show storefront collapse, debris and a thick dust cloud around the dozer.
panels.camera: Aerial camera follows/reframes vehicle across neighboring samples.
panels.action: Wall/roof debris falls and dust expands as dozer moves through the structure.
panels.notes: Presenter rebuts deliberately nonviolent framing and credits reverse-911 evacuation; no casualties shown.

panels.heading: Targets and heavy-equipment resistance
panels.description: Edited aerial footage alternates road travel and a close view of rubble atop the armored shell.
panels.camera: Cuts between overhead street travel and closer vehicle detail.
panels.action: Dozer changes location; rubble rides on shell.
panels.notes: Target names and firing are presenter assertions; no gunfire is visually established by these frames.

panels.heading: Street trees blamed for lost business
panels.description: News footage follows dozer down Main Street near street trees and parked cars.
panels.camera: Aerial tracking/reframing across samples.
panels.action: Dozer travels beside tree-lined frontage.
panels.visualGag: Setup for small-business insanity card and tree-demolition payoff: narrator attributes an owner’s lost trade to irrational blame on street trees, not a verified economic causal claim.

panels.heading: Small business owners are insane people
panels.description: Black card reads SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS / ARE INSANE PEOPLE.
panels.camera: Abrupt cut from news footage to text.
panels.action: Static title card.
panels.visualGag: Editorial punchline to restaurant-owner/tree story; recurs as lesson one at 30:15.7.

panels.heading: Doing a friend a favor by kill-dosing trees
panels.description: News footage returns to dozer pushing into frontage amid trees, rooflines and dust.
panels.camera: Aerial video cuts/reframes closer across samples.
panels.action: Vehicle pushes against frontage; dust/debris increase.
panels.visualGag: Connected payoff to tree-blame setup and insanity card: narrator describes destruction as a favor. Observed frontage destruction does not independently prove each tree’s target status.

panels.heading: Catholic target and explicit IRA callback
panels.description: Green-white-orange graphic reads IRISH REPUBLICAN / ARMY around a black rifle silhouette.
panels.camera: Abrupt static graphic insert.
panels.action: No live action.

sound.text: Third spoken slogan callback, user-confirmed: “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”), after “Unrelated” with the explicitly labeled Irish Republican Army graphic. Raw ASR incorrectly renders “Chucky R. Law.” Coarse cue anchored to source word start1656.84s; not independently measured audio onset. The recurring cutaway gag is not an endorsement of the armed group.

panels.visualGag: Third Catholic-associated cutaway explicitly labels the Irish Republican Army and repeats the user-confirmed “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”) slogan, linking the earlier masked-group and armed-woman inserts; narrator follows with God not being on his side. Running-gag association, not endorsement of the armed group.
panels.notes: User-confirmed third spoken slogan is “Tiocfaidh ár lá.”, not raw ASR’s “Chucky R. Law.” Raw word span1656.84–1657.74s supplies a coarse anchor, not independently measured audio timing. The graphic gives the clearest affiliation cue for the running joke, not historical evidence about Heemeyer’s targets or proof of the graphic’s original source. Raw transcript is unchanged; reviewed display wording comes from the correction sidecar.

panels.heading: Campbell’s and the end of the mission
panels.description: Aerial footage shows dozer pressing into collapsing commercial roof/walls amid dust.
panels.camera: Aerial camera reframes the same destruction across samples.
panels.action: Vehicle becomes surrounded/obscured by building debris.
panels.notes: Presenter says it stuck in a half-basement at Campbell’s, overheated and Heemeyer died by suicide; edited images alone cannot establish exact sequence or interior events.

panels.heading: Getting inside; a hatch all along
panels.description: News footage shows dozer beside damaged building; game model returns after 28:23.9.
panels.camera: Aerial cuts followed by cut back to game.
panels.action: Exterior vehicle/debris footage, then model.
panels.visualGag: Narrated ironic callback to entombment myth: arduous armor-cutting allegedly reveals a hatch all along. No footage of C4 or body recovery is claimed.

panels.heading: Instant folk-hero response
panels.description: Finished game model is toured from overhead down toward Main Street.
panels.camera: Adjacent samples show descent/reframing from high aerial to lower street-facing view.
panels.action: Traffic moves in the model; no historical callers appear.
panels.notes: Presenter recounts sympathetic calls while damage was ongoing and letters to newspaper.

panels.heading: Dozer Day sympathy versus the sanitation cause
panels.description: Game view jumps back overhead and shows rubble-like patches among modeled businesses.
panels.camera: Cut/reframe to overhead model and wider views.
panels.action: Model damage textures/props visible, not live demolition.
panels.visualGag: Narration’s grand folk-hero/festival story is reduced to wouldn’t let him dump poop in a creek; callback to emoji and literal-ditch sequence.

panels.heading: Accommodated, not ruined
panels.description: Game tour moves from wider town to the dirt-road industrial yard now containing a rubble patch where shop assets stood.
panels.camera: Adjacent samples establish changing orbit/viewpoint around yard.
panels.action: Model traffic changes position; ruined yard is static at each sample.
panels.visualGag: The $400,000 sale/free hookup reversals return as argument against the opening ruined-business myth; actual yard model is not financial evidence.

panels.heading: One asshole setup
panels.description: Black card reads IF YOU MEET AN ASSHOLE ONE DAY / YOU MET AN ASSHOLE.
panels.camera: Cut to static title card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the dozen-assholes reversal on next card; prepares narrator’s final literal/metaphorical poop pun.
panels.notes: Presenter vaguely attributes this saying to a cop in a TV show; the show/character and original quotation source are unknown, not established by these text cards.

panels.heading: A dozen assholes payoff
panels.description: Black card reads IF YOU MEET A DOZEN ASSHOLES EVERYDAY / THEN YOU’RE THE ASSHOLE.
panels.camera: Cut to second static text card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to preceding one-asshole setup: repetition reverses blame back onto the aggrieved protagonist; connected to final poop-all-over-everyone spoken line.

panels.heading: Literal and metaphorical poop
panels.description: Game panorama returns near the train station and town streets.
panels.camera: Adjacent samples show viewpoint changing over rail corridor.
panels.action: Train/traffic positions change in model.
panels.visualGag: Narration pays off the asshole cards with eventually pooped all over everyone in more ways than one; panorama contains no invented poop overlay.

panels.heading: Lesson one callback
panels.description: Black card reads 1. ALMOST ALL SMALL BUSINESS / OWNERS ARE INSANE.
panels.camera: Cut to static lesson card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: Explicit callback to 27:11 small-business card, now presented as a mock generalized moral, attributed to presenter.

panels.heading: Don’t shit where you eat expands
panels.description: Second black lesson card lists DON’T SHIT WHERE YOU EAT / OR WHERE YOU WORK / OR IN SOMEONE’S CREEK.
panels.camera: Text list expands between neighboring samples.
panels.action: Additional lines appear.
panels.visualGag: Setup/payoff sequence turns a familiar metaphorical proverb into a literal site-by-site sanitation checklist; full version follows.

panels.heading: An inspected and approved system
panels.description: Expanded card adds illegal sewage tank and ultimately toilet with inspected and approved septic or sewerage system.
panels.camera: Static expanded list; no camera move.
panels.action: Completed text card.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to abbreviated proverb: the comic overlong specificity resolves the entire septic/barrel/ditch/bucket narrative into a genuine public-health rule.

panels.heading: Piracy economics and one-dollar ask
panels.description: Round DNE GOOD FOR ONE FARE logo on black replaces the lesson card.
panels.camera: Static end-brand insert.
panels.action: Logo only.
panels.visualGag: Spoken commercial reverses the piracy premise from opening: more than four minutes seeking a pirated video at $15/hour costs more than the requested dollar; logo itself is branding, not an independent visual gag.

panels.heading: Thanks and patron credits
panels.description: My Patreons heading and three white name columns rise from bottom of black screen.
panels.camera: Locked composition; upward credit scroll established by adjacent samples.
panels.action: Credit text scrolls upward.

sound.text: Credits music identified by downloaded description as Brahms, Tragic Overture Op. 81, Musopen Symphony. Approximate credit-section caption, not a listened exact onset.

panels.notes: Speech ends around 31:36; full source-derived dialogue is retained by shared renderer.

panels.heading: Long credit roll
panels.description: Three densely packed patron-name columns continue scrolling on black.
panels.camera: Static frame with upward text movement across samples.
panels.action: Patron names scroll.
panels.notes: No attempt to transcribe every patron name from contact-sheet tiles.

panels.heading: Final DNE fare-token logo
panels.description: Credits clear and DNE fare-token logo returns centered on black.
panels.camera: Cut/fade transition between sampled credits and static logo; exact transition not resolved.
panels.action: Static ending logo.
